title: Offline metering: sequence-stitching and deterministic reconciliation for air-gapped bundles
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a robust "sequence-stitcher" for on-prem/offline metering bundles so that delayed, out-of-order, or partially-overlapping bundle uploads can be deterministically merged into the central usage ledger without double-counting or under-reporting. This ticket defines the data format changes, local enforcement behavior, reconciliation algorithm, and testing plan for Private/VPC deployments where collectors operate air-gapped and ship batched bundles later (usb/uplink/manifest).
acceptance_criteria: Collector emits a signed bundle manifest with per-tenant monotonic sequence windows and HMAC; server accepts and validates signature and sequence metadata
Server-side stitcher can merge 10k small bundles for a tenant (including duplicates and partial overlaps) and produce a reconciled delta that matches the canonical WAL-simulated ground truth
No usage tokens are double-counted after reconciliation for 99.999% of synthetic runs; any residual mismatches produce an adjustment record and audit trail
Local enforcement honors soft quota while offline and blocks hard quota when local overage risk exceeds configured threshold; policy is configurable per-deployment
End-to-end observability: reconciliation job emits metrics (bundles_processed, duplicates_detected, ordering_conflicts, adjustments_created) and a dashboard workbook is available
Runbook updated with step-by-step recovery for detected ledger divergence and manual bundle replay instructions
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff - scoped algorithm and data model. Decided on per-tenant monotonic sequence ranges (range_start, range_end) in manifest rather than per-record global sequence to reduce per-record overhead.
2025-02-20: Prototype collector manifest v2 (includes tenant_id, range_start, range_end, prev_range_hash, bundle_id, hmac). Implemented HMAC signing with customer KMS stub for POC.
2025-02-24: Server-side validator skeleton implemented. Validator rejects tampered manifests (tested by mutation fuzz). Added schema versioning field to manifest for future upgrades.

2025-02-26: Implemented deterministic merge: prefer lower sequence number; for overlapping ranges, compute intersection and use manifest proof (prev_range_hash) to prefer contiguous sequences and emit adjustment deltas for conflict windows.

2025-03-01: Added idempotency layer based on bundle_id + tenant_id to dedupe replays. End-to-end test harness simulates network delays and out-of-order arrivals; basic reconciliation passes for small test sets.

2025-03-03: Design review with PM and Security. Security asked for stronger auth on manifests (HMAC+timestamp) and retention rules for manifests in S3. Action: add signed timestamp and TTL enforcement in collector and server.
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-metering/pull/529 - stitcher: deterministic merge algorithm and reconciliation worker
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing, HMAC validation, and idempotency dedupe
Fuzz tests with intentionally overlapping ranges and truncated bundles
Large-scale integration test: simulate 10 tenants, 1000 bundles/tenant with randomized delays and duplicates; assert ledger matches source simulator
Chaos test: drop manifests mid-upload and verify bundle replays and dedupe behavior
Staging rollout behind feature flag for 2 weeks; monitor reconcile adjustments and alert on >0.1% adjustment rate
rollout_notes: Collectors: bundle manifest v2 will be behind feature flag; allow mixed-mode (v1 and v2) in server for 6 weeks
Server: reconciliation worker runs as batch job with concurrency cap; increase concurrency gradually while monitoring postgres write amplification
DB migration: add 'bundle_id' and 'manifest_hash' columns to onprem_usage table; run as online migration
Telemetry: tag reconciled delta records with stitcher-run-id for traceability
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: HMAC key compromise on customer side could allow forged manifests. Mitigation: require KMS-backed signing or server-side verification policy; rotate keys and add TTL on manifests.

Risk: Local collector soft-limit may allow large unreported usage leading to big adjustments and customer surprise. Mitigation: add configurable hard thresholds and offline alerting; surface expected adjustment estimate in console.

Risk: Reconciliation worker conflict windows may be large under heavy delayed uploads, causing expensive reprocessing. Mitigation: bound window size; aggregate by tenant shards; apply sampling for large historical mergers and schedule lower-priority background jobs.
Risk: Duplicate bundles from human replays. Mitigation: idempotent bundle_id and strong dedupe logic; include uploader_id and timestamp in manifest for human reconciliation
